newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds little moved, awaiting jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds little moved, awaiting jobs data.

text.p: *Australian bond yields were little changed from Wednesday's close as the market awaited the key labour force report for May at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT).
*June bill futures contract expires at midday.
Australian bond yields were little changed from Wednesday's close as the market awaited the key labour force report for May at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT).
Median expectations are for a moderate employment rise of only 15,000, insufficient to move the unemployment rate which is seen sticking at 8.7 percent, according to a Reuters survey.
"These are fairly critical numbers and could easily shift the short-end 20 basis points either way," one trader said.
A small employment rise, or a negative as one economist is expecting, is expected to renew calls for a further cut in official interest rates.
Conversely, a 35,000 employment increase could spook the short end which is already partially pricing in an easing.
September bills at 94.65 equates to a cash rate of 5.35 percent compared to official 5.5 percent rates, while three-year bond yields are currently only some 60 basis points over cash.

Whatever the outcome of the data, a large proportion of today's turnover is likely to be due to the roll over to September contracts from June. Bills close out out midday today, while three and 10-year bonds expire on Monday.
Meanwhile, U.S. Treasuries were also little changed on Wednesday ahead of May retail sales later on Thursday.
Yield spreads were little changed to the U.S. and Canada, while the local market was outpaced by New Zealand which rallied on a stronger N.Z. TWI and further Eurokiwi issuance.
